I went to the last one, and there was such a variety of prices.
Good. Can you pay by credit card at all the booths?
Some vendors use apps, but not everyone. Maybe stop by the bank on your way.

title: Listen to a conversation.
transcript:
You’re driving to Philadelphia this weekend. Which route will you take?
I’m leaning toward the scenic route, but it’ll take a long time, and my trip is only two days total.
Then why not take the Pennsylvania Turnpike? It’s faster. Even if it’s boring, the tolls from here aren’t too bad.
The highway would save time, but rushing to my destination kind of diminishes the journey.
Maybe take the scenic route there and the highway back.
That’s smart.
Just make sure you leave Philadelphia by 3:00 p.m. or so. Traffic on Sunday nights can be brutal.

title: Listen to a talk in a biology podcast.
transcript:
Have you ever heard of tardigrades? These are animals about half a millimeter in size, just about large enough to be visible to the naked eye. Tardigrades are renowned for their ability to survive a variety of extreme conditions, an ability that is unique among animals. They are found in diverse environments ranging from the deep sea to high mountaintops. They can also withstand temperatures from just above absolute zero to over 150 degrees Celsius. They even survive intense radiation and the vacuum of space.

The secret to tardigrade survival is a process called cryptobiosis. During cryptobiosis, tardigrades lose almost all their water content and produce unique proteins that protect their cells from damage. Remember, metabolic activity—bodily processes—cannot happen without water, so metabolism essentially shuts down. When favorable conditions return, tardigrades rehydrate and resume normal functions.

Scientists are fascinated by tardigrades because understanding their survival mechanisms could have important implications. Take health care, for example. If we can figure out how tardigrades protect their cells from radiation, it might lead to breakthroughs in radiation therapy for cancer patients. Astronomers are also intrigued by tardigrades because of their ability to endure the vacuum of space. In a research study in 2007, tardigrades were sent into space. Some not only survived but successfully reproduced upon their return to Earth. If tardigrades can survive in space, it suggests life might exist in the extreme environments of other planets.

title: Listen to a talk in a film history class.
transcript:
Hollywood, California, is associated with movies. Early Hollywood, through the 1920s or so, was the period of silent films with no recorded dialogue. Maybe you’ve heard of Charlie Chaplin, a famous silent film star. Movies remained silent until the first full-length sound film with spoken dialogue throughout, The Jazz Singer, came out in 1927.

One important filmmaker’s career spanned the silent-film era and later sound films. Her name was Dorothy Arzner. Arzner’s career was unusual for a woman at that time. She started out typing scripts and then editing film. In 1922, she had an opportunity to edit and direct for a silent film called Blood and Sand. It irritates me that she was not credited as an editor or director for Blood and Sand. It’s unfair. She made decisions that saved the movie studio thousands of dollars without receiving acknowledgment.

From there, Arzner made about twenty films and was credited for her work. In fact, she was the first woman to direct a sound film. Many of her films deal with unconventional romance stories—unexpected characters meeting, falling in love, and getting married. Arzner’s films also introduced several women actors who would go on to become successful in comedies and dramas themselves.
